findings.finding: The plan raises the inline-style markup contract to a hard, non-negotiable constraint — 'The element bearing data-figma-id="4478:7209" must declare width:402px, height:874px, box-sizing:border-box, border:0 and padding:0 in its own inline style attribute. CSS classes, stylesheets and <style> blocks do not satisfy this markup contract, even with exact rendered geometry.' — yet CRT-69873d7cb74294f37aadeb68 contains only two GEOMETRY assertions (AST-d3683990ecf1c40d80584969 width=402, AST-ff305af04f3327a5ca31dd35 height=874) whose independent observable is getBoundingClientRect. That measurement is numerically identical for a delivery using the CSS default box-sizing:content-box with no border and no padding, so three of the five mandated declarations (box-sizing, border, padding) have no assertion and no independent proof. The clause stating that exact rendered geometry is explicitly insufficient is therefore unverifiable by any declared obligation: the VISUAL_COMPARE proofs measure only geometry, and the FUNCTIONAL_TEST proofs delegate to implementer-authored assertions in tests/ui.test.js.

findings.finding: PROOF-acf591cc2d754a058eaa1348 states counterfactual properties of the delivered test as part of its expected outcome — 'Presence alone, other dimension values, 100% and 100vh must fail' and 'Dropping the shared import/re-export or hardcoding true must fail' — but its justification and observation are a single execution of implementer-authored tests/ui.test.js on a correct implementation. A passing run observes that the test does not reject a good delivery; it cannot observe that the test would reject a bad one. No declared obligation anywhere in the plan exercises the delivered test against a deliberately wrong implementation. Consequently a weak delivered test (for example a bare substring check for '402px') would satisfy every declared FUNCTIONAL_TEST obligation, and the stated falsification properties would remain certified-by-assertion rather than by observation. The same unobserved counterfactual wording is carried by PROOF-2a56a91ae0a90f4ddd39c2c8 and PROOF-b67b9f48515c35e6dfb2752b and by all three TEST obligations.

The plan makes the title's structural form mandatory — element 4953:6611 must have "exactly one text child strictly equal to 'Zones corporelles', without leading or trailing whitespace or nested elements; substring, trimmed and whitespace-normalised comparisons are insufficient" — but AST-09eea296fefe7a21b29874ab expresses only the Figma CONTENT rule EQUALS "Zones corporelles" (unit TEXT, tolerance 0). The sole independent observable bound to that assertion is the browser's textContent of the title element, which concatenates all descendant text. A delivery such as

Zones corporelles

yields textContent exactly "Zones corporelles" and therefore satisfies both VISUAL_COMPARE proofs while violating the mandated single-text-child / no-nested-element contract. Leading and trailing whitespace are in fact caught by textContent equality; the nesting clause specifically is not. The clause is consequently enforced only by implementer-authored assertions inside tests/ui.test.js, i.e. by the party whose work is under proof, with no independent observation declared anywhere in the plan.
